headline: Burnham Heads to Commonwealth Summit Facing UK Reparations Call
content: Prime Minister Andy Burnham will travel to the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua this week, as the UK comes under growing pressure over slavery reparations.Burnham said ahead of the visit that he rejected calls for financial compensation for slavery — upholding the stance of his predecessor, Keir Starmer — but he indicated a softening of Britain’s position by being open to conversations about reparatory justice, which had previously been ruled out.“We are offering a structured dialogue with those affected by the transatlantic slave trade,” Burnham wrote in the Guardian newspaper in advance of the trip. “Listening to calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British state will form an important part of this process, and I am open to them.”Other leaders due to attend the summit in the Caribbean include Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Australia’s Anthony Albanese, who are both expected to have bilateral talks with Burnham. King Charles III, as Head of the Commonwealth, will address the meeting’s opening on Tuesday.In June, African and Caribbean leaders agreed on a joint approach to seeking reparations for the transatlantic slave trade, in a sign of a more coordinated way forward following a landmark United Nations vote condemning it as a crime against humanity.Over four centuries, an estimated 12.5 million Africans were forced onto slave ships, with about 2 million dying on the way to the Americas and the Caribbean. Portugal transported the most people, followed by Britain, which became the world’s biggest slave trader by the 1730s.“I want to express my sorrow and regret for the pain and suffering of so many millions of people, and to recognize the way it still shapes our world today,” Burnham said in his Guardian piece. “Having these difficult conversations to safeguard the Commonwealth for the future is the right thing to do.”Back in Westminster, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood is expected to announce on Monday how she plans to proceed with controversial reforms to the UK’s immigration system. For almost nine months, the Home Office has been reviewing responses to a consultation on its original proposals, which included a divisive plan to double the baseline time a migrant needs to remain in the country before being able to claim settlement, from five years to 10 — with that timeline reduced for those who were well paid or “contributed” to their local community. Care workers, many of whom came to the UK on worker visas post-Brexit, would see their timeline extended to 15 years. The new rules would apply to anyone already in the country. That retrospective element has angered more than 100 Labour backbenchers, who say the UK should not be changing immigration rules for people who came to work in the country in good faith. While people familiar with the Home Office’s thinking said a concession was likely on Monday, it was unclear whether the Home Office would offer enough to placate concerned Labour MPs.©2026 Bloomberg L.P.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: Austrian paraglider injured in Mandi crash
content: Kullu: A 50-year-old Austrian paraglider pilot was injured after his glider crashed into fields in the Gumma area of Jogindernagar sub-division in Himachal Pradesh’s Mandi district on Sunday.The pilot, identified as Nicholas Thomas, was flying solo from Bir Billing when strong winds in the Gumma hills reportedly caused him to lose control of the paraglider. He crash-landed in fields near Chhanang village, said officials. Thomas sustained injuries to his back, legs and shoulder.Locals alerted the police. As the crash site was inaccessible by road, the injured pilot was carried on a stretcher for nearly one km to the nearest road. headline: 8 labourers electrocuted while working on road-construction project in Rajasthan’s Jhunjhunu
content: Eight labourers were electrocuted when a machine being used during road construction work came into contact with an electricity line in Rajasthan's Jhunjhunu district on Monday, police said, adding that five others sustained burn injuries in the accident.The accident occurred in Chhapoli village under the Udaipurwati police station area, where a narrow road connecting Chhapoli to Kadamkund was being constructed with public participation.Udaipurwati SHO Rampal said a machine being used to mix gravel came into contact with an overhead high-tension power line."The machine came into contact with the high-tension line, causing electric current to pass through it. The labourers working there were electrocuted," he said.He said that eight labourers who died in the accident were local residents.Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma expressed grief over the incident and ordered a high-level inquiry. He sought a detailed report from the district collector and directed officials to ensure prompt and proper treatment of the injured.The chief minister also directed minister Jhabar Singh Kharra to visit the spot and ensure all possible assistance to those affected by the incident.Energy Minister Heeralal Nagar said that according to preliminary information, the road was being constructed with public participation and the work was being carried out privately on a small scale.He said the work was underway on a narrow road connecting Chhapoli to Kadamkund.Nagar said technical officials had been directed to visit the spot and ascertain the circumstances that led to the accident. "If any departmental or technical lapse is found, action will be taken," he said.Former chief minister Ashok Gehlot expressed grief over the deaths and demanded an investigation to determine how the accident occurred and who was responsible.He also urged the state government to provide adequate compensation and all possible assistance to the families of the deceased.Former MLA Rajendra Gudha reached the spot and demanded compensation and a government job for the kin of the deceased.

headline: Soreng, Sikkim: India’s first notified Organic Fisheries Cluster under PMMSY; Union minister launched standard operating procedure for Organic Certification of Fisheries in the Northeastern region
content: The Hon’ble Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh visited Mangan districts, Sikkim on 2nd November 2026 to review fisheries development initiatives under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY). The visit was in line with the structured mechanism for periodic visits of Union Ministers to the Northeastern Region, put in place under the guidance of the Hon’ble Prime Minister to support effective implementation of development programmes in northeast region and obtain field-level feedback. The visit witnessed participation from Shri Puran Kumar Gurung, Hon’ble Minister for Fisheries, AH&VS and Dairying, Agriculture & Horticulture, Government of Sikkim; Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, Secretary (Fisheries), Department of Fisheries, Government of India, High level officials from Sikkim state government, NFBD, ICAR Institutes, fish farmers, fisheries cooperatives and other relevant fisheries stakeholders. the Union Minister visited the Live Fish Vending Centre supported under PMMSY and interacted with members of the Fish Farmers’ Cooperative Societies to understand the challenges faced on ground. Fish feed was distributed to 15 fish farmers from two fisheries cooperative societies, reinforcing support for fish production and farmer-based institutions. The Minister also inspected stalls showcasing fish, ornamental fish and value-added fish products, along with dairy and animal products and locally grown organic vegetables, highlighting the diversity of livelihood and market opportunities in the region. During the program, the Union Minister launched the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Organic Certification of Fisheries in the Northeastern region and inaugurated projects worth ₹375 lakh under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), encompassing critical fisheries infrastructure such as hatcheries, feed mills, cold storage facilities and production-related technologies such as Biofloc and Recirculatory Aquaculture system (RAS). The projects inaugurated under PMMSY will strengthen critical links across the fisheries value chain. Kisan Credit Cards were distributed to fish farmers for facilitate access to institutional credit, while cheques were provided to five fish farmers under the Mukhya Mantri Matsya Uthpadhan Yojana (MMMUY), further strengthening financial support for fish farmers and fisheries-based livelihoods. The Government has adopted a cluster-based approach for integrated development of the fisheries value chain, bringing together production, processing, value addition and marketing within identified geographical areas. Under PMMSY, 34 fisheries production and processing clusters have been notified across the country, including organic fisheries clusters in Sikkim and Meghalaya. Soreng District, Sikkim is India’s first Organic Fisheries Cluster launched under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY). The cluster focuses on ecologically healthy fish farming without the use of harmful chemicals, antibiotics and pesticides, with special emphasis on Amur carp, Indian Major Carps (IMC) and Trout. It seeks to build on Sikkim’s established organic ecosystem while strengthening the fisheries value chain, enhancing incomes of fish farmers and creating opportunities for premium domestic and international markets for organic fish and fish products. The SOP for Organic Certification of Fisheries in the Northeastern region will further strengthen this ecosystem by providing a structured framework for organic production and supporting traceability across the value chain. By developing a more credible and market-oriented organic fisheries ecosystem, the initiative will enhance the positioning of organic fish products and support their access to premium domestic and export markets. Sikkim has taken a pioneering step towards strengthening market linkages by entering an MoU with Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) for institutional procurement of locally produced Rainbow Trout. The initiative seeks to provide a stable market for trout farmers while strengthening the value chain for this high value Coldwater fish. The proposed arrangement envisages regular supply of trout to ITBP establishments, with emphasis on quality specifications, supply capacity, pricing, inspection and supply schedules.

headline: PM-SETU to strengthen North-East's skilling ecosystem through industry-led ITI transformation; Tourism and Hospitality identified as key sectors for global employment opportunities
content: The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India, organised a programme on Skilling for International Mobility & PM-SETU', with a special focus on the Tourism and Hospitality sector in Guwahati today. The programme brought together senior representatives of the Central and Assam Governments, industry stakeholders and the skilling ecosystem to deliberate on strengthening the North-Eastern Region's skilling infrastructure, expanding international employment opportunities for its youth and fostering industry-led transformation of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) under the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU). The programme highlighted the immense potential of the North-Eastern Region in tourism and hospitality, particularly in the context of the growing demand for skilled professionals in domestic and international markets. Discussions focused on aligning skill development programmes with emerging industry requirements, international standards and opportunities for global workforce mobility. Delivering the keynote address, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India, highlighted the importance of aligning India's skilling architecture with the changing requirements of industry and the global economy. He emphasised that initiatives such as PM-SETU are aimed at bringing industry closer to skill development and training, ensuring that ITIs evolve into modern, demand-driven institutions capable of preparing young people for emerging opportunities. "India's strength lies in the aspirations and capabilities of its youth. Through PM-SETU, we are working towards transforming our ITIs into modern, industry-responsive institutions that equip young people with skills relevant to the future of work. The North-Eastern Region has enormous potential, particularly in tourism and hospitality, and our endeavour is to ensure that its youth are not only prepared for opportunities within the country but are also equipped to participate confidently in the global workforce."

headline: Wildflower Hall Shimla: Oberoi Group Secures 35-Year Lease Of Heritage Hotel
content: The Oberoi Group, through East India Hotels Limited (EIHL), will continue to operate and manage the iconic Wildflower Hall near Shimla for another 35 years. The Himachal Pradesh government has awarded the group the licence to operate the luxury heritage hotel after it submitted a record bid of 47.1 per cent of the hotel's annual gross revenue.Located in Chharabra, around 12 km from Shimla, Wildflower Hall has been managed by EIHL for nearly four decades. The latest agreement follows a competitive e-auction conducted by the state government, which had invited tenders in June 2026 for the property's operation, management and maintenance.According to Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, the agreement is expected to generate approximately INR 2,000 crore in revenue for the state over the 35-year licence period.Himachal Pradesh To Earn INR 2,000 Crore Over 35 YearsAnnouncing the outcome of the e-auction, Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said the government expects to earn approximately INR 3 crore per month from the property, with a 3 per cent annual increase over the licence period.In addition to the revenue share, the agreement includes an upfront licence fee of INR 24 crore and a commitment from the Oberoi Group to invest at least INR 50 crore in the hotel's property. The state government has also received approximately INR 400 crore in cash through the property, according to the Chief Minister.The government has clarified that the agreement does not involve the transfer of ownership. The land, hotel property, joint venture company, associated assets and rights will remain under the full ownership and control of the Himachal Pradesh government. The new arrangement grants EIHL the rights to operate and maintain the hotel.A New ChapterThe latest agreement comes after nearly 25 years of legal disputes over the ownership and management of Wildflower Hall. The partnership between the state government and EIHL was terminated in March 2022 over alleged contractual violations, leading to a prolonged legal battle that went from the Himachal Pradesh High Court to the Supreme Court.In February 2024, the Supreme Court ruled in favour of the Himachal Pradesh government and directed that ownership and control of the property be restored to the state. The government officially regained control on March 31, 2025.Following this, the Department of Tourism and Civil Aviation invited fresh tenders for the hotel's operation and maintenance. A pre-bid conference was held in July 2026, ahead of the competitive e-auction.The state government has described the latest arrangement as an important step towards generating revenue from the property while retaining ownership of its land and assets.The Story Behind The 123-Year-Old Wildflower HallSet at an altitude of 8,250 ft, Wildflower Hall is one of India's best-known luxury mountain resorts. Spread across 77,471 sq m, the property has 85 rooms, a spa, a swimming pool, a gymnasium, and banquet facilities. Its grounds are also home to more than 2,200 trees, most of them mature deodars.The property's history dates back to the late 19th century, when it was owned by GHM Batten, private secretary to the Earl of Lytton. After the original building was destroyed in a fire, it was reconstructed by Batten. Lord Kitchener later acquired the lease, and the property eventually changed hands before being developed into a three-storey hotel with 37 rooms in 1925.After Independence, the property was taken over by the Centre and used as an agricultural school until 1973. It was subsequently handed over to the Himachal Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation for hotel operations.The building was destroyed in another fire in 1993, following which the state government invited global tenders to redevelop it as a five-star hotel. This led to the association with East India Hotels Limited and the creation of Mashobra Resorts Limited, through which the property was managed.With the new 35-year agreement, Wildflower Hall enters another chapter in its long history, with the Oberoi Group returning as its operator under a fresh arrangement with the Himachal Pradesh government.(With inputs from various sources)FAQs1. Who will operate Wildflower Hall in Shimla for the next 35 years?East India Hotels Limited (EIHL), part of the Oberoi Group, has secured a 35-year licence to operate, manage and maintain Wildflower Hall following a competitive e-auction conducted by the Himachal Pradesh government.2. Has the Oberoi Group acquired ownership of Wildflower Hall?No. The agreement grants the Oberoi Group operating and management rights. Ownership and control of the hotel's land, property, joint venture company, associated assets and rights will remain with the Himachal Pradesh government.3. Where is Wildflower Hall located?Wildflower Hall is located in Chharabra, approximately 12 km from Shimla, at an altitude of around 8,250 ft.4. How much revenue is Wildflower Hall expected to generate for Himachal Pradesh?According to Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, the agreement is expected to generate approximately INR 2,000 crore for the state over the 35-year licence period.5. What are the terms of the new Wildflower Hall agreement?The agreement includes an upfront licence fee of INR 24 crore, a revenue share based on 47.1 per cent of the hotel's annual gross revenue and a commitment from the Oberoi Group to invest at least INR 50 crore in the property.Oberoi Group To Develop 20 Wellness-Focused Luxury Resorts Across India And Overseas
